features: A UTILITY BILL WITH A CREDIT LINE NOW REGISTERS — Invoices containing a reducing line — the “system charges” credit that gas and electricity bills carry inside the document — were rejected with “Accounting integrity error: imbalance detected between DEBIT and CREDIT”. On a real bill with a −€ 1.80 line at 22%, the sum of the lines came to € 104.54 against a document total of € 100.15: the reducing line was counted at its absolute value, so it was added instead of subtracted — the difference counted twice. The document now registers, and the expense chapter shows the true total consumed.

REVERSING THOSE INVOICES NO LONGER INFLATES THE CREDIT NOTE — Reversing an invoice with a reducing line produced a credit note worth more than the invoice it was meant to cancel: € 134.20 against € 109.80 in a verified case. That left € 24.40 of credit towards the supplier matching no real money, and the chapter ended up with negative spending that flowed into the statement and was shared among the owners. The credit note is now an exact mirror of the invoice, and the two documents cancel out to zero.

REOPENING ONE OF THOSE INVOICES NO LONGER GROWS IT SILENTLY — On the edit page the reducing line appeared without its minus sign: € 10.00 instead of −€ 10.00. Simply reopening the invoice to fix a date and saving it pushed the total from € 109.80 to € 134.20, loading the chapter with € 24.40 that was never spent — with no warning, and with the bookkeeping still balancing.

A DOCUMENT WITH A NEGATIVE BALANCE IS NO LONGER REJECTED — When line credits exceed the charges (a credit adjustment larger than the period's consumption), the document is worth less than zero: the supplier owes us, not the other way round. Registration used to fail with the same imbalance message. It now registers, with the supplier debt on the correct side of the ledger.

REVERSING A PRIOR-YEAR INVOICE NOW ACTUALLY WRITES TO THE JOURNAL — Reversing an invoice recorded as prior-year debt produced an EMPTY credit note: the invoice was marked as reversed, the document was created at zero, and the debt stayed on the balance sheet with nothing flagging it. The credit note is now worth as much as the invoice it cancels, and the accounting entry is written.

REDUCING ADJUSTMENTS NO LONGER BECOME CHARGES IN THE INSTALMENT PLAN — When generating an extraordinary instalment plan from an invoice containing a reducing adjustment, the quota engine ignored its sign: on a € 1,000.00 document with a −€ 200.00 adjustment it generated quotas for € 1,400.00. Owners paid 40% more than the document. Fixed: the adjustment now reduces the quotas instead of increasing them.

A NEGATIVE LINE AMOUNT CAN NO LONGER BE TYPED ON A CREDIT NOTE — On a credit note the sign is already set by the document type: typing one by hand cancelled it out, turned the total positive again, and made the program stop recognising it as a credit note — it became payable and reversible like any ordinary invoice. The restriction is now in place and, more importantly, visible: the message appears under the amount field and explains why. On an ordinary invoice a reducing line remains allowed, because there it is legitimate.

IMPORTING A FILE FROM A PREVIOUS FINANCIAL YEAR NO LONGER MEANS RETYPING THE AMOUNT — An electronic invoice dated in a closed financial year is recorded as prior-year debt, and that panel asks for a single amount. As long as the import sent only the detail lines, that field stayed at € 0.00: on six real files out of eleven the administrator had to retype by hand an amount the file already declares — the opposite of what the import promises. The amount and the rate now come from the document.
